clicked: HUDs, menus, signs, mic and webcam, X posts.

blocks.text: A HUD is only what the player needs this second: the game's main readout (speed, health) big, a second number smaller below, each on a small plate, readable across the room, no bigger (40–56 px at 1080 p). No word floats pale on the scene: a plate under it or a stroke. One grid: every plate 24 px from the edge, edges meeting neighbours'. The game's name lives on the page; controls are learned once from a fading hint in the first seconds; rules, by playing. A win or loss is a moment in the world first (→game-feel), then the number and play-again on a plate beside it. Control words are labels (turn, actions.<name>.label) that follow rebinds, never key names; one unlike the declared key is the player's rebind (mouse 4/5: side buttons): keep it. Arrival, identity and voice are Spawn's: the play press and first click or key start sound and take the mouse, a player is their Spawn name and face overhead and on every board, talk is Spawn's mic (join, mute, open or hold V →social), so a game builds no click-to-start or tap-for-sound gate, mic button, nickname or login; asked, say so and build just a sign-in button on player.isGuest. The game owns its fiction (named character, hero or team on player.state). A game opens in the world: a start screen (title, lobby) empties the room; never add or remove one unasked (ui.startScreen). A level pick is a pad, doorway or marked area to stand on, a portal only to another place (→portals); a character or loadout pick, a station to walk to. A plate holds what reads like a page and wears one edge; a changing value moves. The screen is in the game's material: the engine's pixel face: Jersey 10, Geist Pixel Square (Grid/Circle/Triangle/Line stripe small text) named by world.config.yaml's engine.ui.theme.font, or its own (spawn upload an open-licence .woff2 named in @font-face): the world's palette, flat fills, hard edges, a hard-offset shadow (the plate below), never a web page's glass card; system-ui throws the face away.

UI work runs from a mock: look, then spawn paint "<the finished screen: each plate, its words, its place>" --ref <address beside the frame> edits the frame into the mock (their pictures as more --ref); one say shows it (!the mock) as you start, no question. Build to the mock in ui.js; a piece it put in the rail moves; say so. look again; the closing say shows before and after.
spawn paint "<the finished screen: each plate, its words, its place>" --ref <address beside the frame>

// ui.js is one module on the page: the engine calls the default export whenever what it reads moves, ≤30/s (a glide is CSS; read ctx.now() only to draw time); every named export is a page global for onclick const THEME = ``; export default function (ctx, player) { const s = player.controlling?.state ?? player.state, turn = ctx.world.inputs.axes?.moveX?.label; return `${THEME}
SPEED
${Math.round(s.speed ?? 0)}
SCORE
${s.score ?? 0}
${turn ? `
${turn} to steer
` : ""}
`; }

A later screen (results, shop) stands in every render, hidden until shown: the engine draws it before play. Nodes match by id: a kept id keeps its running animation; a new id or changed inline animation replays it. A stamp in a keyframes or class name is whole (Math.round(s.at)): ctx.now() has a fraction, whose dot breaks the name. A loop moves only opacity or a transform; stroke-dashoffset and others repaint every frame: a glow pulses the opacity of a shadowed ::after at inset:0, never scaled or larger (a shadow leaves its box dark); marching dashes slide a repeating-linear-gradient strip. A render throw blanks the HUD until one succeeds. Secret cards are owner rows under their player →platform-systems. Theme classes paint, utilities place: .plate sets no position or display (authored rules beat utilities) and is no utility's name (ring: a blue box-shadow).

The rail is Spawn's: one block centered on the right edge, every platform and width; never hide, move or cover it: its rows are var(--spawn-chrome-reservation-right-top) / var(--spawn-chrome-reservation-right-height), above and below them the edge is the game's; a plate or scrollbar across them clears its band (right: calc(var(--spawn-chrome-reservation-right-inset, 50px) + 24px)), a centered line there pads both sides alike or ends above it (bottom: calc(100vh - var(--spawn-chrome-reservation-right-top) + 24px)).

Escape frees a locked cursor and closes Spawn's chat: a game opens nothing on it or the release (pointerLockLost), even asked; its bound action fires. A game's menu, pause and HUD buttons take its own keys, each printed; pause sets ctx.place.timeScale: 0 holds every body, timer and effect.
html { cursor: none } hides the arrow over the whole game; url(…), auto draws its own.

A hotbar scroll is two actions mouse: "wheelUp"/"wheelDown" (a pulse per notch), never the wheelY axis. Real buttons keep pointer-events-auto. Plates fit a 390 px phone: side by side they flex-wrap, none narrower than its one-line label; a panel across the band's rows clears it on both sides, the HUD under it hides; on touch its words name the tap (✕); past ~640 px tall it scrolls.

WORDS on a thing are big letters on its bare material (
HIGH TOWN
, a colour the material is not). A PANEL (readouts, buttons) is a FLOATING PLATE: a bare root with a margin holds a soft-edged plate in its place's material. A SCREEN the ui draws (an arcade game) is material.canvas. HTML a door or lid uncovers is a face too: the page frame trails moving 3D. A plate that FOLLOWS a thing (nameplate, marker) is HUD HTML with data-world-anchor="": atop its body, or at data-anchor-offset="x y z" metres from its feet; --anchor-depth is metres away for a CSS fade.

data-modal = "this surface owns the screen" (dialog, story card, bag or shop), one at a time: the cursor frees while shown, relocks after; siblings dim, unclickable; one title bar, the card's; an always-shown bar carries none. Invisible still catches clicks and costs an iPhone a screen-sized layer: panel-less backdrop, idle hit marker or spent intro is visibility:hidden.

An icon is a painted picture: one spawn paint "" --size 1024x1024 per icon, each slot-sized; an inline ). HTML holds no sound or sound setting but one mute (→audio). ctx.view.site ("x.com" on X, "" unnamed): fit the frame, no mouse lock.
Microphone and camera (getUserMedia), SpeechRecognition and navigator.geolocation share the platform's ask (surface its reject or error); never gate on track.muted.

// ui.js's page side; in the render ctx.self is the body's handle (player.controlling's while set), ctx.session a plain copy sendAction(name, payload, { down, relockPointer }) // down true on pointerdown, false on pointerup = a held button; relockPointer = back to mouse-look ctx.emit("haptic", { kind: "light" }) // a press's buzz from its action's handler in the player's script, the presser's alone; the Spawn app and a controller buzz, a phone browser never sendAxis(name, value) // into input.axes. openLink(url) // opens discord.gg or spawn.co, confirmed, ≤3/min; other URLs are copyable text, no download onMount(container, player) / onDestroy(container) // container = #tome-game-mount, empty viewport-wide pointer-events-none layer beside the render's #tome-ui-container: getElementById finds render nodes audio.context, audio.bus("UI" | "SFX" | "Music"), audio.buffer(ref) // in onMount: the HUD's own WebAudio graph (a press tick: an oscillator) into the bus, under the rail dials window.spawn.assets.upload({ blob, name }): { url } // a player's or image/audio/video bytes (GLB if .isEditor) become a /cdn/ url to store, never base64; the game's link with ?card= unfurls as that picture; e.code guest_not_allowed, rate_limited (wait e.retryAfterSeconds when set) window.spawn.user.upgradeGuest() // Spawn's sign-in window.spawn.view.captureFrame({ type, quality, maxSize, camera?: ViewCamera }): Blob // screenshot/photo, no HUD; code capture_unavailable = no frame yet navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia({ audio: true }) // that view and sound; no picker, screen or system audio; preferCurrentTab adds UI window.spawn.chat.sharePicture({ blob, scope }): { url, width, height } // the player's picture, checked by Spawn, said as them in chat or a chat.js scope; paint url with , never a copy; refused: code rejected, message for the player window.spawn.on("event", (name, payload) => …) // in onMount: each ctx.emit("uiEvent", { name, payload }) once: an effect, never a persisted value; onDestroy calls the returned unsubscribe data-interactive // marks a custom element clickable (buttons, links, inline handlers are) spawn-canvas // one element, the game's viewport: its box alone gets the picture's resolution; no transform, clip or pointer events; backdrop: box-shadow 0 0 0 200vmax #000 ctx.worldToScreen(position): { x, y, depth, onScreen } | null // one-shot placement at a static point; null off-client ctx.world.engine.ui.referenceHeight: number // the design's window height (1080); fixes a HUD huge or tiny ctx.self.inputHeld: boolean // true while Spawn's chat, menu or held Tab has the keyboard: the render or body script holds a clock or pad read on it navigator.getGamepads(), navigator.languages // ui.js only: each controller apart; an action names each button it reads, or a key or mouse action takes it var(--spawn-safe-area-top|right|bottom|left, 0px) // notch insets on html var(--spawn-touch-corner-band-height, 0px) // bottom-right touch buttons' height over the safe-area bottom; the stick owns bottom-left
